set menu = a limited list of dishes offered at a fixed price
tasting menu = a sequence of small dishes chosen by the chef
sommelier = a restaurant specialist who advises on wine
service charge = an extra percentage added to a restaurant bill for staff
cover charge = a fixed fee some restaurants add per person before food
table manners = the polite way of eating and behaving during a meal
aperitif = a drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite
mocktail = a mixed drink without alcohol
fully booked = having no free tables left
walk-in = a customer who arrives without a reservation
fine dining = formal, high-quality restaurant food and service
street food = ready-to-eat food sold from stalls or carts
food truck = a vehicle from which cooked food is sold
sharing platter = a large plate of food designed for several people to share
overpriced = costing more than it is worth
value for money = worth the price you pay because of quality or quantity
food critic = a journalist who reviews restaurants and dishes
signature dish = the recipe a cook or restaurant is best known for
chef's special = a dish recommended or created by the chef that day
dietary requirement = a need to avoid or include certain foods for health or belief
